display_title: [AutoPGLE] Sync devices after profiler startup.

head_commit.message:
[AutoPGLE] Sync devices after profiler startup.

This improves measurement quality by removing host-side variability in
when the executable is actually launched under the profiler from the
measured cost of (typically) the first collective in the executable.

Costs are prefixed by the executable fingerprint, so the cost of the
barrier kernel will not pollute the measured costs for the executable of
interest even though it will be captured by the profiler.

Make sure that executables compiled with the same device mesh shape but
different concrete device lists get different PGLE profilers, which is
important now that the PGLE profiler owns a barrier prepared for the
specific set of devices.

display_title: Reimplemented `gpu_info` using `jaxlib._gpu_spec`

head_commit.message:
Reimplemented `gpu_info` using `jaxlib._gpu_spec`

The vast majority of the diff is from #39469 by vfdev-5@.

A few things to highlight:

* The GPUs available for AOT are limited to the XLA GPU specs, and the
  abstract device kind has to match a spec's device description exactly,
  e.g. "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3" rather than "NVIDIA H100".
* `registry` is removed, so there is no way to register a custom `GpuTargetConfig`.
* For the local GPU, `get_gpu_info` works with or without a spec, because
  the config is built from the device's attributes on the fly.
* There is no public API for this feature yet.

Merging this change closes #39469

display_title: Fix array base broadcasting in jnp.logspace

head_commit.message:
Broadcast a non-scalar base in jnp.logspace as NumPy does

jnp.logspace passed `base` straight to `power` with the linspace result,
so a non-scalar `base` was matched against the trailing dimensions of the
output instead of being broadcast with `start` and `stop` and expanded
along `axis`. Depending on the shapes this gave the wrong shape (a scalar
`start`/`stop` with a length-3 `base` gave (3,) instead of (3, 3)), paired
bases with the wrong start and stop values, or raised an error.

Do what NumPy does: bring `start`, `stop` and `base` to their common rank
and insert `axis` into `base` before taking the power. The scalar `base`
path is unchanged.

display_title: [JAX:GPU] Migrate Triton FFI custom call to XLA FFI KernelRegistry.

head_commit.message:
[JAX:GPU] Migrate Triton FFI custom call to XLA FFI KernelRegistry.

Registers compiled Triton kernels with XLA's FFI KernelRegistry during Initialize and launches the registered kernel for stream execution and command buffer recording. The Initialize handler is now required.

For autotuned kernels, Initialize registers every candidate so that Execute can find the winner's handle. Autotuning itself still loads the candidates through the old path until the follow-up, so for now autotuned candidates are loaded twice.

Kernels with num_ctas > 1 no longer get the CU_CLUSTER_SCHEDULING_POLICY_SPREAD hint when launched directly but this is not used when launched inside a cuda graph already so it reconciles behavior.

Kernels launched by the FFI handler are now owned by the XLA executable and unloaded with it, instead of being cached for the lifetime of the process.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007273840

head_commit.message:
Remove absl::StatusOr from xla::ifrt::Array::pjrt_layout().

No `xla::ifrt::Array` implementation returns errors from `pjrt_layout()` except `BasicStringArray`, which returned `absl::UnimplementedError`. Returning `nullptr` from `BasicStringArray::pjrt_layout()` instead lets `Array::pjrt_layout()` return `absl_nullable std::shared_ptr<const xla::PjRtLayout>` directly and removes unnecessary error-handling boilerplate from callers.

head_commit.message:
Merge jax-ml/jax main into woa_support

Resolve conflicts in build/requirements_lock_*.txt by taking main's lock
files and re-resolving them with `python build/update_requirements_uv.py
--no-upgrade`, so all package versions match main and only the Windows
ARM64 environment markers differ.

Also fix the tensorflow/jax/jaxlib markers in build/requirements.in:
`sys_platform != "win32" and platform_machine != "ARM64"` excluded all of
Windows (including x64) and all ARM64; use
`sys_platform != "win32" or platform_machine != "ARM64"` so only Windows
ARM64 is excluded, matching the numpy/scipy markers.
